generator.construction: Create degree copies (stubs) for each labeled vertex; Fisher-Yates shuffle with rejection-sampled bounded integers; pair consecutive stubs; reject any self-loop or repeated undirected edge; sort/canonicalize accepted edges; validate every vertex has exact requested degree.
generator.output_format: DIMACS edge format, one-based vertices, canonical sorted edges
generator.retry_policy: default maximum 100000 pairings per instance; the cap may be configured lower per run; exhaustions are explicit failures and must not be silently retried with a new seed
generator.caveat: Deterministic generation is not itself evidence that a sample is independent or distributionally representative. Test generator statistics before confirmatory use.

resource_limits.rationale: The largest planned paper-shaped case is 5,000 vertices at degree 3 (15,000 stubs). The ceiling prevents accidental huge allocations through the public generator API.
resource_limits.raising_policy: Any increase requires explicit review and documented memory/throughput evidence.

canonical_source.note: Source pin includes generator exhaustion errors that retain n, degree, seed and max_attempts, plus a structured JSON failure receipt emitted to stderr by the CLI while preserving DIMACS-only stdout. Rust remains uncompiled in this environment.

motivation.primary_reference: Wybo et al., Scalable quantum-enhanced greedy algorithm for maximum independent set problems, accepted by Physical Review Research on 2026-10-19
motivation.scope: Independent random-regular graph benchmark track; not a reproduction claim until the accepted paper's complete methods and parameter files are captured.

split_design.size_holdout: Validation and test sizes are never used for selector tuning. Test sizes 2048/4096 target graph-size generalization beyond train sizes.
split_design.leakage_caveat: All instances share a random-regular generator family; this measures size generalization within the chosen graph family, not out-of-distribution generalization to other graph distributions.

seed_derivation.purpose: Stable, non-overlapping deterministic workload seeds; seed values are recorded explicitly per workload below.

pre_registered_arms: strong classical local-search / iterated-local-search baseline with per-run and aggregate budget disclosed
the published QAOA-informed minimum-degree greedy configuration, after its angle source, QAOA depth, marginal estimator and hardware settings are independently captured
randomized classical greedy/local-improvement negative controls with the exact seed schedule
quantum-informed-reduction policy as a separate algorithm track rather than silently merged into QAOA-informed greedy
physical-QPU, ideal-circuit, tensor-network simulation and replay evidence stored as distinct arms
preregistered_metrics: MIS cardinality and relative/absolute gap to a proven optimum when available
objective distribution across graph and replicate, not only the best run
shots, batches, circuits, preprocessing, compile/transpile, calibration, queue, classical compute, QPU time and end-to-end wall time
graph generation overhead reported separately from solve-time metrics, with generation included only when the deployment use-case requires on-demand generation
release_gates: Compile and run generator unit tests locally; preserve compiler/toolchain version.
Generate each workload once, validate exact degree/simplicity, and pin raw DIMACS SHA-256 and byte length.
Validate generation seed replay byte-identically and record attempts_used.
Run a generator-quality audit over graph isomorphism-insensitive and degree/triangle/connectivity statistics before confirmatory comparisons.
Freeze all method configurations and test-size outcomes before selector tuning.
Record failures, timeouts, rejected-generation exhaustion and infeasible outputs rather than dropping rows.

paper_shape_replication_scale.caveat: Matches the preprint's reported graph sizes/sample counts, but uses new derived seeds rather than the authors' exact graph instances. The preprint's graph seed list/source instances were not found in its public page at inspection time, so this is replication-scale independent sampling, not exact graph-for-graph reproduction.
paper_shape_replication_scale.p1_negative_control: At p=1, the authors derive equivalence to the classical minimum-degree greedy choice (uniform random tie-breaking); verify that the implementation reproduces this on every test fixture before interpreting p>1.
paper_shape_replication_scale.qaoa_fixed_angles: Pin the precise tree-derived parameter values from the preprint appendix/cited fixed-angle source before any run labelled reproduction.
paper_shape_replication_scale.hardware_evidence_caveat: The preprint describes p=2/p=3 IQM Garnet measurements. For some p=3 light cones requiring 21 or 22 qubits on a 20-qubit device, it substituted noiseless simulated expectations; label those runs mixed hardware/simulator evidence, not hardware-only.

classical_sota_comparison_campaign.reference_algorithm: Marino and Kirkpatrick linear-time prioritized search for random d-regular graphs
classical_sota_comparison_campaign.algorithm_under_test: fixed-angle quantum-enhanced greedy with depth p=4
comparison_requirements: Keep two designs distinct: same-completed-graph paired comparisons for graph-conditioned solvers; original Marino-Kirkpatrick deferred-decision comparison is unpaired at the distribution level unless identical completed-graph inputs are actually verified.
Do not label an input-conditioned adaptation of Marino-Kirkpatrick as the original algorithm; if implemented, pin and evaluate it as a distinct variant.
Add ordinary minimum-degree greedy as a control, including the p=1 identity control.

Freeze separate seed streams for the generator-coupled Marino–Kirkpatrick procedure and fixed-graph QGreedy cohort; record one raw output row per generated graph. For graph-conditioned arms, record one row per shared graph digest and method.

Pre-register N<=2000 as the primary reproduction comparison because the preprint reports statistically significant improvement through that range; report N=5000 as a separately labelled scaling result.
Measure independent-set cardinality and ratio |I|/N across graph instances; do not treat an asymptotic independence-ratio bound as the exact optimum of each finite graph.

Report total CPU time and every QAOA/physical-shots/circuit/queue/calibration/setup cost. Amortize reusable precomputed light-cone expectation tables across the exact number of workload instances served, and report break-even volume.
Keep actual QPU measurements, tensor-network expectations, replayed published outputs, and classical emulation in separate evidence classes.

cohort_relationship.extension_96: The existing 96-workload split across degrees 3/4 and held-out sizes is an extension/generalization track, not the paper's 3-regular replication-shape cohort.
cohort_relationship.paper_shape_1400: A separate seeded 3-regular cohort with the seven sizes and 200 instances per size reported in the public preprint.
cohort_relationship.sota_campaign_700000: A specified larger streaming campaign (100000 graphs per size) for the Marino-Kirkpatrick SOTA comparison; it has not been executed and should not be conflated with the 1400-graph replication-shape set.

fixed_instance_solver_panel.estimand: difference in verified independence ratio/quality when each algorithm receives the identical completed graph
algorithms: p=1 fixed-angle QAOA-informed greedy identity control, which should reduce to minimum-degree greedy with randomized tie handling
p=4 QAOA-informed greedy using a pinned expectation-value source and distinct simulator/physical-QPU evidence
ordinary minimum-degree greedy with predeclared tie-breaking
seeded multi-start minimum-degree greedy with all restarts and total runtime charged
fixed-instance classical local-search or ILS baseline, with declared time/iteration budget
fixed_instance_solver_panel.pairing_unit: graph SHA-256 plus preregistered repetition seed; graph is the outer statistical cluster
fixed_instance_solver_panel.inference: paired graph-level effects; cluster-aware uncertainty; correct preregistered multiplicity
fixed_instance_solver_panel.evidence_boundary: The original Marino-Kirkpatrick deferred-decision procedure is not included in this paired panel unless a separate completed-graph solver variant is implemented and explicitly labelled as a new variant.

generator_coupled_distribution_compariso.estimand: difference in independence-ratio distributions over the same declared random simple d-regular graph distribution, with graph/independent-set construction coupled in the Marino-Kirkpatrick arm
generator_coupled_distribution_compariso.reference_algorithm: Original Marino-Kirkpatrick deferred-decision prioritized procedure, source and compilation provenance pinned separately
generator_coupled_distribution_compariso.comparison_to_qgreedy: Unpaired distribution-level comparison. The algorithms do not consume identical completed graph bytes: Marino-Kirkpatrick discovers edges as part of constructing the graph and uses those partial labels to decide future pairing/virtual-node actions.
generator_coupled_distribution_compariso.do_not_do: Do not assign a shared graph-pair key or run a paired sign-flip test between original Marino-Kirkpatrick outputs and QGreedy outputs unless exact same-graph identity is actually established.
required_controls: Verify the paper's uniform simple d-regular generation contract and rejection behavior; no loops or parallel edges in accepted graph samples.
Use preregistered size/degree cells and report sample counts, seed ranges, failed attempts and graph statistics for each arm.
Report unpaired mean/median independence ratio, distribution quantiles, uncertainty and runtime/cost with a correctly specified independent-sample analysis.
Compare the finite-N results to the published asymptotic lower-bound reference r_infinity approximately 0.445330 as a theory line, not as a same-instance observation.
Keep N<=2000 primary and N=5000 scaling/sensitivity separate as preregistered by the paper-shaped track.

comparison_designs.compatibility_rationale: Marino-Kirkpatrick (arXiv:2003.12293, Section 2–3) uses deferred edge revelation and generates the random d-regular graph concurrently with its label/virtual-node process. It claims uniform sampling under constrained stub pairings. It is therefore not natively a function from arbitrary completed graph input to MIS solution. A fixed graph input-adapted implementation is a different algorithm and must have a different ID.

paper.title: Large independent sets on random d-regular graphs with fixed degree d
key_sections: Section 2: deferred-decision generation of random simple d-regular graphs
Section 3: deferred-decision prioritized algorithm for d=3

reference_repository.license_note: The inspected source has copyright notices and no explicit open-source license was found in the pinned repository tree. Treat it as all-rights-reserved; do not copy or redistribute source into Symthaea without permission. Use it as a referenced executable baseline only if usage/permission is cleared. Prefer an independently written implementation from the published algorithm if a code port is required.

marino_kirkpatrick_prioritized_search.compatibility: Original algorithm constructs graph and independent set jointly through deferred edge revelation. It is not automatically a fixed-input MIS solver for arbitrary pre-materialized graph files.
marino_kirkpatrick_prioritized_search.source_identity_scope: Git commit and Git object IDs pin the source snapshot; they are not SHA-256 raw file digests.

generator_quality_evidence.seed_stream_note: Canonical PR #8324 implementation was aligned to the preflight seed stream: same XorShift64* generator, rejection-sampled Fisher-Yates bounded draws, and in-place re-shuffle of the stub vector between rejected attempts. Byte parity must still be verified by compiling/running Rust.

canonical_rust_generator.seed_stream_semantics: XorShift64* plus rejection-sampled Fisher-Yates; the canonical generator shuffles the stub vector in place between rejected attempts, matching the JS preflight's specified deterministic stream semantics.
canonical_rust_generator.execution_status: not compiled or executed; JavaScript preflight does not substitute for Rust tests or byte-parity verification
